newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end lower, wine stocks sparkle.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end lower, wine stocks sparkle.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed softer for the fifth session in a row, although wine stocks bounced on hopes of a surge in exports to the United States and Canada, said traders.
The bolsa is seen stable on Wednesday with stocks expected to rise Thursday on bargain-hunting, they said.
The 40-share IPSA index ended down 0.12 percent at 94.57 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.07 percent to 5,167.73 points amid volume of 10.5 billion pesos.
Wine stocks sparkled on expectations that exports to the U.S. will rise sharply this year as disease has damaged vines and hurt harvests in California, said traders.
Exports to Canada are also seen rising following the signing of a free trade agreement between Chile and Canada, they said.
Concha y Toro, Chile's largest winery, soared 9.14 percent to 191 pesos on foreign buy orders, said dealers.
Other wineries which firmed included Emiliana, up 3.38 percent at 42.5 pesos and San Pedro which rose 2.67 percent to 2.31 pesos.
Fears that the $450 million Genesis Chile Fund will sell part of its stock portfolio continued to undermine the market, they said.
Denials from Genesis officials in Chile that the fund was liquidiating its portfolio have only partially managed to calm investors, said traders.
Losers included fertilizer-maker Soquimich, down 3.52 percent at 2,190 pesos, Banco O'Higgins, down 2.17 percent at 1,580 pesos and power utility Chilgener, which lost 1.35 percent to 2,200 pesos.
